title: gateway: admission control middleware + standardized overload errors (Retry-After)
author: Amara Diallo
release_notes: Hosted API: during overload the gateway now performs feature-flagged admission control and returns consistent 429/503 responses with Redwood overload codes and Retry-After.
description: Context: As part of ENG-4821/ENG-4822 we need deterministic overload behavior and consistent error semantics at the edge (before requests fan out into routing/runtime). Today overload often manifests as ambiguous 5xx/timeouts and client retry loops. This PR adds an API gateway middleware that (1) classifies requests (tier, route/model, streaming vs non-streaming) and (2) evaluates admission control (local + routing hint) to either forward or shed early with a standardized overload error payload including Retry-After. Scope: Hosted endpoints and OpenAI-compat endpoints in the gateway only (no changes to runtime scheduling in this PR). Behavior is behind feature flags and defaults to pass-through. Decision notes: - Error mapping follows ADR-0147 draft: return 429 when rejecting due to policy/rate-like admission decisions; return 503 when upstream capacity/breaker indicates temporary unavailability. - Always include Retry-After when we shed (integer seconds) to reduce retry storms; default values are conservative and can be tuned per region/model. - Responses include `x-redwood-overload: 1` and `x-redwood-error-code` to make client handling/metrics deterministic. - For streaming: if admission fails, we fail before opening the stream (do not mid-stream inject an overload error). Implementation: - New middleware `AdmissionControlMiddleware` runs after auth and before request proxying. - Adds request classification derived from resolved route/model (if present), customer tier, and request type. - Introduces a small interface `AdmissionEvaluator` with two implementations: `NoopEvaluator` (default) and `RoutingHintEvaluator` (calls routing control plane for a shed hint if enabled). - Standard overload error builder used for both REST and OpenAI-compat response paths, including JSON body shape and headers. - Adds metrics counters and duration histograms for admission decisions with bounded labels (per Allison’s cardinality review). Rollout: - Feature flags: `gateway.admission_control.enabled`, `gateway.admission_control.routing_hint_enabled`, `gateway.admission_control.retry_after_seconds_default`. - Flags can be set per region and per route group. - Logging includes a sampled structured log line with decision + reason code to support oncall triage. Testing: - Unit tests for header/body mapping, status selection, streaming preflight rejection, and OpenAI-compat error shape. - Integration test using `gateway-test-harness` verifying upstream is not called when shed is active. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Wire breaker state store into routing hints (ENG-4824/4825) - SDK surfacing of `Retry-After` and overload codes (ENG-4836) - Ensure billing/quota paths treat overload-shed requests as non-billable (tracking with Cole; partially covered in logging here).
illustrative_snippet:
Example response when shedding (Hosted REST):
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
content-type: application/json
retry-after: 2
x-redwood-overload: 1
x-redwood-error-code: OVERLOAD_UPSTREAM_CAPACITY

{"error":{"type":"overload_error","code":"OVERLOAD_UPSTREAM_CAPACITY","message":"Service is temporarily overloaded. Please retry after 2s.","retry_after_seconds":2,"request_id":"req_01H..."}}
commits: gateway: add admission control middleware scaffolding + flag plumbing
gateway: request classification (tier/route/streaming) and decision context
gateway: standardized overload error builder + headers (Retry-After, x-redwood-*)
gateway: metrics + sampled logs for admission decisions (bounded labels)
tests: unit + integration coverage for shedding + streaming preflight behavior
review_conversation: Brian Murphy (review): Can we ensure the JSON body shape matches what we want in ADR-0147, especially for OpenAI-compat? Also please confirm we never return a raw upstream 502 when we decide to shed at the edge.

Amara Diallo (author): Yep. Edge shed path now always uses `buildOverloadErrorResponse()` for both hosted + openaiCompat. Upstream 502/504 are untouched in this PR (still proxied) but when we shed locally we do not emit 502; only 429/503 per mapping. Added unit tests validating the OpenAI error object includes `error.type`, `error.code`, `error.message` and includes `Retry-After` header.
Christine Wong (review): For Retry-After, please add a note on how we pick seconds and avoid flapping. Also request classification: are we labeling metrics by raw model name? Cardinality risk.

Amara Diallo (author): Updated: Retry-After is configurable; default is 2s for upstream-capacity shed and 1s for policy-based shed. Added jitter note in docs comment and ensured we can override per region via flags. For metrics: we label by `route_group` (bounded enum) and `tier` + `request_kind` only. Model name is not a label. Added a test ensuring `route_group` defaults to `unknown` if not resolved.
Allison Grant (review): Please remove `customer_id` from logs/metrics. Structured logs are fine but keep them sampled and do not include PII. Also ensure `request_id` is present for correlation.
Amara Diallo (author): Removed `customer_id` from the log payload. Logs are sampled at 0.01 by default and include `request_id`, `tier`, `route_group`, `decision`, `reason_code`, `retry_after_s`.

Mina Haddad (review): RoutingHintEvaluator should time out aggressively and fail open; we can’t have gateway threads hanging. Also can we plumb a response header so we can distinguish routing-driven sheds from local policy sheds in support tickets?

Amara Diallo (author): Added 35ms timeout + circuit breaker for the routing hint call; failures default to allow. Added `x-redwood-shed-layer: gateway|routing_hint` header only when shedding (not on allow).

Cole Summers (review): Billing hooks: any chance this increments request counters for rejected requests? We need shed requests to be non-billable and ideally not counted as usage. If not addressed, at least add an explicit audit log field so we can reconcile.

Amara Diallo (author): Gateway currently emits usage events only after upstream response; since we shed before proxy, no usage event is emitted. Added explicit `admission_decision=reject` field to the access log line so we can confirm in pipelines. Tracking deeper billing alignment separately.
Brian Murphy (approval): Looks good after the OpenAI-compat test additions. Approving.
Christine Wong (approval): Approved with the timeout/fail-open change.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved; thanks for removing IDs and bounding labels.
Mina Haddad (approval): Approved; routing hint timeout is the key.
